as_read: One 244-person RCT in functional dyspepsia met its primary outcome at 1920 mg/day, rated low certainty by Cochrane; lipid and fatty liver results favor extract on surrogates; labels print 500 to 750 mg a serving, so no credit is recommended for a human ruling, and this one deserves a real look.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: sum score of weekly rating of overall change in dyspeptic symptoms
studies_to_add.quote: The primary efficacy variable was the sum score of the patient's weekly rating of the overall change in dyspeptic symptoms (four-point scale).

stop_list: Six label rows (18368, 30958, 288774, 307554, 294008, 295528) carry canonical_id artichoke, not globe_artichoke, so labels.py prints no row for them; the amounts came from reading those product rows directly. Two ids for one ingredient looks like a defect for the main session to check.
Label directions for servings per day were not read; the dose gap is per serving only.
Whole herb extract on DSLD 269954 is outside the leaf extract tested.
clinician_items: 41274796: transaminases, particularly AST, increased in the extract group of 40 bariatric candidates with obesity and steatotic liver disease; the authors note this differs from prior studies. Pooled analyses (35763310, 41270328) and 29520889 report ALT and AST falling, so these conflict.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_moderate rests on 14653829, which is accurately described. Cochrane 37323050 rates the artichoke result low certainty on 1 study of 244 participants. Purpose matches only the digestive labels.
